The Moment We're In

Jewish teens are being asked to defend who they are.

In classrooms, online, and among peers, they encounter distorted history, denial of Jewish peoplehood, and antisemitism disguised as political discourse. Even teens active in Jewish life may lack a clear understanding of Jewish history and Israel's centrality to Jewish identity.

This program supplements — not replaces — existing Jewish educational opportunities. And it uniquely reaches teens who aren't currently engaged at all.

"We cannot expect young people to stand confidently in their story if we have not first helped them know it." — Haviv Retig Gur

The Program

Three sessions. One community.
A story they can claim.

Dynamic, immersive gatherings at The Barry Family Campus — designed in partnership with local educators, powered by StandWithUs, built for every Jewish teen in the Twin Cities.

01

October 2026 — Launch

Israel 101

The historical and ideological roots of Zionism, the significance of Israel as a Jewish homeland, and how Jewish holidays, prayers, and practices are tied to Eretz Yisrael. Teens explore how Jews are indigenous to the land — and why Zionism is the most successful Land Back movement in human history.

02

Winter 2027 — Session 2

Combating Antisemitism

The many forms of antisemitism — historical and contemporary — and the tools to identify and respond to it in daily life and on campus.

Session 03 · Spring 2027 — Culminating Event

Tell Your Story

Teens synthesize what they've learned into their own story, presented in a gallery walk open to families and the wider community — reflecting on their journey and demonstrating what knowing your story makes possible.

What Teens Take With Them

The goal is not to hand them
talking points — it's to help them think for themselves.

Stronger Knowledge

A clear understanding of Jewish history, Israel, values, and peoplehood grounded in fact.

Sense of Belonging

Relationship building across synagogues, schools, and backgrounds — community as the product.

Language & Confidence

The ability to identify misinformation, reject false choices, and participate in hard conversations.

Complexity & Compassion

Hold nuance — support Israel, care deeply about others, stay grounded in Jewish values.

Questions

A Few Things
You Might Be Wondering

Who is Know Your Story for?

Every Jewish teen in the Twin Cities, grades 8–12 — regardless of denomination, affiliation, or how connected they currently feel to Jewish life. It's built especially for teens who aren't already deeply engaged.

What's the time commitment?

Three sessions across the 2026–2027 school year, plus the culminating Tell Your Story gallery event in spring 2027.

Does my teen need a Jewish education background?

No. Sessions are designed to meet teens where they are, whether they've had years of Jewish schooling or almost none.

Is there a cost?

Details on cost and any financial assistance will be shared closer to launch.

How do I get my teen involved?

Reach out to knowyourstorymn@gmail.com or use the Get Involved button below — we'll follow up with registration details.

A Community Effort

This only works if we build it together.

Know Your Story is innovated by local Jewish educators, professionals, and volunteers, and brought to life in partnership with community organizations across every movement and denomination.

The goal is not to duplicate or recreate what already exists. It's to do together what none of us can do alone: reach every Jewish teen in the Twin Cities and give them what they need before they leave for college.
